title: The Mysterious Story of Larry Bader
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck (with an iHeart intro voice) tell the strange story of Lawrence Joseph "Larry" Bader, an Akron, Ohio man who vanished on Lake Erie in May 1957 while boating out of Rocky River, Ohio, was declared dead in 1960, and then resurfaced in 1965 in Omaha, Nebraska as "Fritz Johnson," a local TV sports director and archer. FBI fingerprints matched him to Bader's Navy records. The episode covers his family's reaction, the legal and financial fallout, the dissociative fugue explanation proposed by the hosts, his death in 1966, and a listener mail shout-out for a grandmother named Nana.
topics: Stuff You Should Know listener mail

segments.title: Opening
segments.summary: Show opening and hosts introduce the episode.

segments.title: Larry Bader's early life and career
segments.summary: Larry Bader is introduced as a charming, Catholic, well-to-do Akron native born in 1926. He served in the Navy from 1944, attended the University of Akron briefly, married Mary Lou Knapp in 1952, and worked as a cookware salesman while carrying debts and unpaid taxes.

segments.title: Debts and reputation
segments.summary: Bader's debts, unpaid taxes and milk bill are described, along with friends' accounts of him as a fun, likable family man.

segments.title: Departure for Cleveland and boat rental
segments.summary: On May 15, 1957, Bader paid bills including a life insurance premium that had been changed to add an accidental death payout, told his pregnant wife he might go fishing, and rented a boat at Eddie's Boat Dock in Rocky River, Ohio, from Lawrence Cottrell, paying extra for running lights.

segments.title: Storm and disappearance on Lake Erie
segments.summary: Bader was seen by the Coast Guard heading out before a storm. The boat was found about five miles away, undamaged except for scratches and a bent propeller, with life jackets aboard. Bader was never found despite a search of a couple of months.

segments.title: Search, hosts' Lake Erie anecdote, and death declaration
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the search, a rumor about the cash, and a personal anecdote about Lake Erie drownings at Kelleys Island. Bader was declared dead in 1960, and his wife collected a $40,000 insurance payout and Social Security.

segments.title: Transition to Omaha
segments.summary: The hosts recap and introduce the next thread: a man named John Johnson arriving at the Round Table Bar in Omaha three days after Bader vanished.

segments.title: John Johnson arrives in Omaha as Fritz
segments.summary: A man calling himself John Johnson, also called Fritz, appeared in Omaha eight hundred miles away, claiming to be a Navy veteran and orphanage alumnus. He resembled Bader, got a job at Ross's Steakhouse, and quickly became a local figure.

segments.title: Fritz's eccentric lifestyle and archery
segments.summary: Fritz bought a hearse converted into a lounge, wore a leather beret, hosted parties, and won Nebraska archery titles. He eats a whole chicken, bones included, as a party trick.

segments.title: Radio job and quirky habits
segments.summary: Fritz got into radio through a friend at KBON and became a DJ reading news. Other quirks included signing checks with just the season and his name, and a bartender tip-deposit anecdote.

segments.title: Fritz's later career, marriage, and eye patch
segments.summary: Fritz married model Nancy Zimmer in 1961 and adopted her daughter, had a son, moved to KETV as sports director, consulted for archery companies, and wore an eye patch after losing his left eye to a tumor.

segments.title: Ad break
segments.summary: Mid-episode sponsor break.

segments.title: Party tricks banter
segments.summary: The hosts and iHeart voice trade jokes about the chicken-eating trick, the hat-on-the-wall trick, and breath-holding fainting games.

segments.title: 1965 discovery in Chicago and fingerprint match
segments.summary: In February 1965, an acquaintance saw Fritz at a sporting goods show in Chicago and identified him as Bader. Niece Susannah confronted him, the family flew to Chicago, and FBI fingerprint comparison with Navy records matched. Fritz said he was shocked and did not know the other man.

segments.title: Hosts discuss inconsistencies and the family's fallout
segments.summary: The hosts note Fritz's odd choice of a new identity in a large city, and that his life was not falling apart. The attorney Harry Farnham arranged psychological and neurological exams that found nothing medically wrong. Mary Lou's life was upended, and Fritz lost his TV job, marriage, and money.

segments.title: Consequences for Mary Lou, Nancy, and Fritz
segments.summary: Mary Lou had remarried plans and faced insurance and Social Security repayment demands. Fritz moved to a YMCA and sent money to his families. Mary Lou and Fritz met in Chicago and Nancy left the scene.

segments.title: Akron Beacon Journal coverage and Fritz's death
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a September 1965 Akron Beacon Journal article written in a Hunter S. Thompson style. Fritz is quoted about God solving the problem, and he died of cancer on September 16, 1966. He had a memorial in Omaha and was buried in Akron.

segments.title: Dissociative fugue explanation
segments.summary: The hosts explain dissociative fugue, a rare condition involving sudden retrograde amnesia and a new identity, and debate whether it fits Bader's case. Chuck proposes a theory involving a traumatic event at sea, and they note the usual duration is weeks or months.

segments.title: Listener mail: shout-out for Nana
segments.summary: A listener named Nori requests a shout-out for her 81-year-old grandmother, a longtime fan, who wishes to attend a live show. The hosts suggest a show near her home in Omaha.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh invites listener mail and the show credits iHeartRadio.
